did_you_know.text: Did you know? David had six sons born in Hebron: Amnon, Daniel, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, and Ithream; the text also gives the names of their mothers.
Did you know? David reigned in Hebron for seven years and six months, and then reigned in Jerusalem for thirty-three years.
Did you know? According to the text, David’s sons born in Jerusalem were Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon—four sons born to Bath-shua, the daughter of Ammiel.
Did you know? At the end of the list of David’s sons, the sons of his concubines are also mentioned, although their names are not given, along with Tamar, their sister.
Did you know? The line of the kings of Judah in this chapter continues from Solomon through Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, and Jehoshaphat, to Josiah.
Did you know? Josiah’s sons are listed in order: Johanan the firstborn, Jehoiakim the second, Zedekiah the third, and Shallum the fourth.
Did you know? After Jehoiakim, the list continues with Jeconiah and Zedekiah, describing the continuation of the dynasty during the period shortly before the exile.
Did you know? Zerubbabel is mentioned as the son of Pedaiah, and Zerubbabel’s children are listed as Meshullam and Hananiah, along with their sister Shelomith.
Did you know? The list continues through Hananiah, Shecaniah, Shemaiah, and Neariah, showing how the genealogy extends across many generations.
Did you know? At the end of the chapter, seven sons of Elioenai are listed: Hodaiah, Hodaiah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.
